note: Length limits and sweet spots per platform and per format. `max_s` / `min_s` are the platform's own limits where it publishes them; `aim_s` is a sweet spot: published only where `aim_grade` says platform, otherwise a practitioner range or the pack's house default. No platform publishes an ideal length for organic posts. Limits change: re-check the source before a hard-fail rule. Narrative and named examples: docs/evidence/launch-video-patterns.md#lengths.

grades.platform: the platform's own help or spec page
grades.practitioner: editors, creators, agencies, vendors; or press relaying a platform without a primary page

youtube.shorts.note: square or vertical uploads up to 3 min are Shorts (from 15 Oct 2024); a Short over 60 s with an active copyright claim is blocked, which matters for a music bed you do not own

youtube.longform.note: no published ideal length; 25 s is the minimum for an end screen; key moments need >= 60 s and 100 views; chapters need >= 3 timestamps of >= 10 s

youtube.ad.skippable.note: no maximum; under 3 min recommended; billed as a view at 30 s (or the end if shorter) or on interaction

instagram.reels.note: 3 min per press reports of the 20 Jan 2025 change; the help page did not render for us
instagram.reels.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

instagram.reels.ad.note: 9:16 at 1440 x 2560 recommended; safe zone: keep text out of the top 14%, bottom 35% and 6% each side

tiktok.organic.note: TikTok publishes no ideal length; longer uploads were tested for some accounts; the in-app upload screen shows each account's limit
tiktok.organic.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

tiktok.ad.infeed.note: non-Spark in-feed ads up to 10 min; no recommended duration; the creative guide puts the hook in the first 6 s and the proposition in the first 3 s

x.free.note: 2:20 for accounts without Premium (X's help page blocked our fetch; read from a search summary of it)

x.premium.note: up to 4 h at 1080p on web and iOS (search summary of X's help page)

linkedin.organic.note: 3 s on desktop, 2 s on mobile, up to 15 min (search summary of LinkedIn help)

linkedin.ad.note: 15-30 s recommended so the ad qualifies for every feed placement; in-stream ads up to 90 s

trailer.theatrical.note: corpus mean of 6,926 trailers of 4,004 top-grossing films 1930-2025; the 150 s cap is a voluntary trade rule reported by the trade press
trailer.theatrical.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

teaser.note: explainers and editors; exceptions run past 2 min
teaser.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

launch.social.note: launch-video studios recommend 30-60 s for social and 60-90 s for a site demo; a public gallery of launch videos posted on X read on 2026-10-16 had a median of 72 s (our count of 53 entries; runtime did not separate high-view from low-view entries)
launch.social.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

founder.launch.note: practitioner guidance: founder on camera, no music for the first 12-20 s
founder.launch.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

podcast.clip.note: clip tools score windows of about 25-60 s
podcast.clip.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

lesson.chunk.note: median engagement capped at about 6 min whatever the length (6.9M sessions in four online courses, 2014); segment lessons under 6 min; tutorials are re-watched and skimmed, so chapter them
lesson.chunk.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

business.video.note: completion falls with length: one business-video host reports 66% completion under 1 min, 56% at 1-2 min and 50% at 2-10 min (2022 data); another reports engagement roughly flat from 1 to 5 min, then a drop
business.video.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

ad.cutdowns.note: the house cut-down set for every ad: a 6 s bumper, 15 s and 30 s
